The general pattern in the embedding literature is that gains flatten out somewhere around 100 to 200 dimensions for most tasks. Continued gains are more plausible when the graph is large, the downstream task has many classes or fine-grained labels, and the training data is rich enough (for example, more or longer random walks) to populate the extra dimensions. Under those conditions, longer walks supply more co-occurrence context, so higher dimensions can keep helping. With short walks, the extra dimensions tend to add little or overfit, so the benefit of higher dimensionality depends on walk length.
